alex: heads-up — seeing repeated 200–800ms tail spikes on p99 token latency from replica-3 during long-context jobs. looks KV cache is doing strange stuff under sustained long sequences :eyes:

alex: dump from the worker around spike (trimmed):
```
replica=replica-3 worker=kv-pager pid=4821 event=evict_scan duration_ms=1213 entries_scanned=18432 evicted=0 reuse_hits=2 fragmentation_pct=38 mem_delta_mb=+512
replica=replica-3 worker=kv-pager pid=4821 event=paging duration_ms=245 queue_len=18
```

alex: note "evicted=0" while mem_delta is positive — looks like we scanned but didn't reclaim. repeating across 3 spans.

sara: can you repro with a trace and flamegraph? need to know whether lock contention or allocator churn.

alex: repro steps: run long-context load test (context_len=120k, warmup 50 reqs, then sustained 5qps tails). attaching perf profile command I used: `perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30` then `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded && flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg`

alex: flame shows big blocks in `evicter::scan()` and a hot inner in `arena_alloc::maybe_compact()` — looks like fragmentation-triggered compaction while scan is trying to evict.

jin: this smells like LRU metadata thrash. Under bursty insertion patterns, our LRU lists get constantly reordered and hamstring the fastpath. FIFO would avoid pointer-churn but we've seen reuse regressions earlier.

maria: from the correctness side, FIFO caused a small window where a recently-used entry could be prematurely evicted -> reproducible for certain long-context rollouts (one of our canaries failed with alignment errors). need to be careful. :thinking:

casey: quick experiment idea: smooth the eviction threshold with exponential decay so scans don't run hard on short bursts. pseudo: `watermark = max(min_wm, ema(prev_wm, current_usage, alpha=0.2))` and trigger evict only when usage > watermark + hysteresis. keeps us from thrashing on transient spikes.

casey: also add a fast-path check to avoid compacting arena during eviction scans: if `evict_scan_in_progress` then skip `maybe_compact()` and schedule compaction later. reduces simultaneous compaction+scan overlap.

jin: might help. but need to validate tail tradeoff: smoothing raises steady-state watermark and could increase memory tail. want a config knob per pool.

alex: CI log shows perf regression around commit `a3f9b2c` (changed kernel selection heuristics to favor large-batch kernels). ci-bot: `CI: perf/regression p99 +18% on kv-heavy loads (a3f9b2c)`

ci-bot: failing test: `kv_long_context_stress` — artifact at `artifacts/1719005432/trace.json`

maria: large-batch kernel change explains it — batching increases per-request KV allocations (more KV entries created per token batch), which amplifies insertion rate and floods LRU metadata path.

sara: so this is an interaction bug: batching heuristic change -> higher instantaneous insert rate -> eviction scan runs concurrently -> compaction + scan thrash -> no reclaimed entries -> memory ticks up -> latency spikes. we should add a regression test for that interaction.

casey: proposed short-term mitigations: 1) revert kernel bias for the affected job-type or limit `max_batch_size` for KV-heavy routes, 2) enable smoothing/hysteresis behind feature flag, 3) add a post-scan compaction rate limiter.

jin: for correctness check: we need an invariant assertion in CI: after an eviction scan, `mem_delta_mb` should not be positive unless evicted>0 OR compaction scheduled. add a sanity metric.

alex: action list:
- alex: run canary with smoothing flag on replica-3 (will push tonight)
- sara: add flamegraph-driven CI check and the invariant assert in `kv_pager_tests`
- jin: run FIFO vs LRU microbenchmark under high-insert bursts and collect reuse stats
- casey: draft PR with smoothing + disable-compact-during-scan change

maria: one more note — we also saw KV key aliasing in long contexts (prefixes slightly mutated) preventing reuse. separate follow-up: consider prefix-normalization or a compaction pass to dedupe hot prefixes.

alex: ok pushing canary now. will post results in ~30m. thanks all :thumbsup:

casey: small snippet to toggle flag in prod-config: `kv.eviction.smoothing.enabled=true` and `kv.eviction.smoothing.alpha=0.25`

jin: for the microbench, use this harness: `go test -bench=BenchmarkKVInsertBurst -run=^$ -benchmem` with `-args maxEntries=100000 burstRate=2000` and collect `reuse_hits` metric.

alex: canary result: p99 dropped from +350ms to +40ms after smoothing + disabling compaction during scan. memory tail reduced but not fully flat. posting graphs: (internal link)

maria: good progress. leaving a note to track long-term: 1) evaluate hybrid LRU/FIFO for different hotset shapes, 2) consider per-shard watermarks instead of global to avoid cross-shard spill, 3) KV compaction background worker that respects throttle.

sara: will open follow-up tickets and prioritize tests. flagging infra for a scheduled rollout window. :hammer: 

alex: thanks team — keeping this thread sticky until we merge the smoothing PR. :party_parrot:
